title: Tell, do not ask
description:
This `Stock` class hands its data out and lets anybody put it back, so every caller has to remember the rules ("never below zero") and one day somebody will forget:

```cpp
if (stock.getQuantity() >= 3) stock.setQuantity(stock.getQuantity() - 3);
```

Redesign it so the object looks after its own rule. Remove the setter. Offer **actions** instead:

- `explicit Stock(int quantity)` (a negative start becomes 0),
- `int quantity() const`,
- `bool take(int amount)`: removes that many and returns `true`; if there are not enough (or `amount` is not positive) it changes nothing and returns `false`,
- `void restock(int amount)`: adds that many; amounts that are not positive are ignored.
rules: Remove the setter: outside code should not set the quantity directly.

rules.message: Remove the setter: outside code should not set the quantity directly.
